papers.title: Evacuee's diary
lines: The volcano grumbled for two years before it spoke. Then it covered the capital in ash.
We left the south and moved north. Some went to England. We remember Plymouth as it was.

papers.title: Postcard home
lines: They call it the Emerald Isle of the Caribbean, and the Irish saints day is a public holiday.
I wore green and danced to a steel band. I have not been so happy since Dublin.

trail.clue: A farmer buried a small tin of EC dollars near the open ground in the nineties, 'in case of ash'.

papers.title: Observatory log
lines: Dome growth continues. Pyroclastic flow at 14.03. We watch with cups of tea and caution.
The mountain does not care. We care for the mountain, with sensors, patience and the occasional prayer.

papers.title: Goat water recipe
lines: Goat water is the national dish: stewed goat, cloves, breadfruit, dumplings, a splash of the volcano's good humour.
Eat it hot. Eat it with friends. Do not tell the goat.
